summary: Exeter sits at the western base of the Sierra Nevada foothills, roughly halfway between Fresno and Bakersfield along the San Joaquin Valley's eastern edge — and from its compact 2.5-square-mile footprint, you can look east toward the Sequoia National Park entrance less than forty minutes away, a proximity that no other valley-floor town of its size can quite match. The citrus industry still anchors the local economy, with orange groves pressing right up against residential blocks, and the town's outdoor murals painted on downtown buildings have become a minor regional attraction. At a median home price of $273,500 against a median household income of $71,198, the price-to-income ratio lands around 3.8 — genuinely affordable by California standards, though the 17.2% poverty rate signals that wages across the economy run modest. With 9.4 hours of daily sunshine on average and daytime highs that push well past 100°F in summer before cooling to mild, fog-prone winters, the climate rewards early risers and punishes midday errands from June through September. The town has no major hospital or corporate campus, so most higher-paying employment means a commute — Visalia is about fifteen minutes west along Highway 198. Exeter is a place where the cost of housing is remarkably low and the mountains are remarkably close, but the tradeoff is an economy scaled to a small agricultural town, not a regional job center.
